top.title: Crypto Exchange Gemini Sells U.K. and EU Units to KAST for Under $10 Million
top.description: Bitcoin Magazine Crypto Exchange Gemini Sells U.K. and EU Units to KAST for Under $10 Million Gemini Space Station has sold its already shuttered U.K. and European operations to Singapore stablecoin payments firm KAST for less than $10 million, according to CoinDesk reporting , as the exchange prepares to report third-quarter results after Thursday’s close. Gemini declined to comment. A spokesperson for KAST would not discuss the transaction, but said the company is actively looking at acquisitions as its revenue and footprint grow. Neither firm has issued a public confirmation of a sale, and no regulator has announced a change-of-control approval. The disposal, if confirmed, would close a retreat Gemini laid out in February. On Feb. 4, the Nasdaq-listed company, known as Gemini (GEMI), approved a plan to exit and wind down its operations in the United Kingdom, the European Union and other European jurisdictions, and Australia, as part of a broader effort to cut expenses and support a path to profitability. It said it would keep operating in the United States and Singapore. The plan included a reduction in force of up to 200 employees in Europe, the United States and Singapore, or about 25% of Gemini’s global workforce as of that date. The company estimated about $11 million in pre-tax restructuring charges, mostly in cash, and said it expected the wind-down to be substantially completed in the first half of 2026. Reuters reported the job cuts the same day. Co-founders Cameron and Tyler Winklevoss, who started Gemini in 2014 as a bitcoin exchange, told customers the firm would “double down on America” after foreign markets proved hard to win and stretched the company’s cost base. Gemini later told U.K., European Economic Area and Australian customers that their accounts would close on April 6, with withdrawals-only starting in early March. What would change hands in a sale is the leftover entities, staff and regulatory permissions from those already wound-down units, not Gemini’s core U.S. exchange. Buyers of shuttered crypto businesses often want the licenses more than the remaining operations. Any transfer of a licensed firm in the U.K. or the EU typically still requires a change-of-control review by local regulators before a new owner can run it. A payments firm with European ambitions KAST is a Singapore-based financial platform built on stablecoin rails. In March, it said it had raised $80 million in a Series A round co-led by QED Investors and Left Lane Capital. The company, founded in July 2024 by former Circle executive Raagulan Pathy, said it would use the capital for expansion, licensing and compliance. KAST provides dollar-denominated accounts, cross-border payments and cards that let consumers and businesses hold, move and spend stablecoins. top.title: Man Utd sack manager Carrick, with Pochettino set for hot seat
top.description: Michael Carrick has paid the price for Manchester United's disastrous start to the season (Oli SCARFF) Manchester United sacked manager Michael Carrick on Thursday after their worst-ever start to a Premier League campaign, with USA boss Mauricio Pochettino widely tipped to replace him. Former United captain Carrick led the team to an impressive third-place finish last season, but they have taken just eight points from 10 games in the current campaign and are in the relegation zone. The club confirmed in a statement that it had parted ways with the 45-year-old, following mounting speculation he would be axed during the international break. "After a disappointing start to the season, the club has come to the extremely difficult conclusion that a change is necessary in order to achieve our ambitions," United's statement said. "Michael is, and always will be, a Manchester United legend. Just as he did as a player, he has conducted himself with the highest standards of dedication and professionalism throughout his time back with the club." United said they intended to appoint a permanent successor "as quickly as possible". - Chaos - Carrick impressed after taking over as interim boss following Ruben Amorim's acrimonious exit in January, leading United to Champions League qualification. He was rewarded with a two-year permanent deal but, hampered by the club's underwhelming recruitment in the summer transfer window, his side have endured a steep decline this season. Carrick has struggled to maintain discipline, dropping captain Bruno Fernandes after he criticised his manager's tactics following a 4-1 thrashing at Champions League debutants Como. And defender Lisandro Martinez spoke out against the club's hierarchy over their lack of top-quality signings. Carrick's final game in charge was a chaotic 4-4 draw against Aston Villa on Sunday, after which he stressed he would not walk away. United, however, have decided to act in the hope of saving their season after a paltry three wins from 15 games in all competitions. It is believed Carrick's future was decided on Wednesday during a meeting in Monaco involving co-owner Jim Ratcliffe, chief executive Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox. Ex-Newcastle boss Eddie Howe and Julian Nagelsmann, most recently in charge of Germany, were touted as possible replacements but Pochettino has now emerged as the overwhelming favourite to succeed Carrick. The Argentine has extensive experience of the Premier League following spells in charge of Southampton, Tottenham and Chelsea, and he also coached Paris Saint-Germain. Pochettino signed a contract extension to remain with the USA through to the 2030 World Cup just three months ago. - 'Legend' - But Sky Sports reported Wednesday that United have "reached a verbal agreement in principle" with Pochettino, who has been linked with a move to Old Trafford on several previous occasions, to become their new boss. top.title: Marlon Gomes: “Brazil have always been my second home”
top.description: Marlon Gomes: “Brazil have always been my second home” For someone who faithfully represented Brazil from the ages of 15 to 20, a two-year absence may have felt like an eternity. Between 2019 and 2024, Marlon Gomes played for Brazil’s Under-16, Under-17, Under-18, Under-20 and Under-23 teams. With that kind of history, the path to the senior national team seems natural. Called up for the first time, the midfielder—matured by his journey “in his second home,” by overcoming the challenges of becoming a father at 15, and by the resilience needed to stay focused while playing in a country at war—now finds himself on the team he has always dreamed of playing for. “I spent a lot of time here, going back to the youth teams. I started coming to the national team at 15, so it has always been my second home. Whenever there was a call-up, I was there, along with Andrey. I have many friends I’ve known since the youth teams, and I’m very happy to see them again and to return (to the national team) after a long time, now with the senior team,” he said at a press conference on Thursday (12). Playing for Brazil, the Rio de Janeiro native won the South American Under-20 Championship and competed in the Under-20 World Cup and the CONMEBOL Pre-Olympic Tournament, as well as international friendly tournaments. Marlon Gomes at a press conference in Singapore during his first call-up to Brazil’s senior national team Credits: Rafael Ribeiro/CBF Experienced at youth international level, this time he is one of the newcomers among the 25 players selected by Carlo Ancelotti for the friendlies against Japan and Singapore. “I’m happy about this new project to bring fresh faces into the national team. I’m very happy, and my expectations about returning to the Brazilian national team couldn’t be higher. Now I’m fulfilling a dream with the senior team and being part of this new cycle. I have the highest hopes. This is my first time here. I hope to train well and learn as much as possible from the big-name players, and I hope I can play well so I can come back more often,” he said. A father at 15 A product of Vasco’s youth system, which he joined in 2017, Marlon Gomes became a father at a young age. His daughter Maitê was born when he was 15—a challenging age for someone who would have to balance fatherhood, the daily demands of football training and travel, and the dream of changing his family’s life. Despite the difficulties, he was determined to keep the promise he made to his mother and his daughter’s mother to grow personally and professionally. "I was very young and didn’t have the financial means. When my mother found out, we all cried together: me, her and my daughter’s mother. I promised to change our lives, and not just with empty words, but by becoming a great player and a respectable young man who would make it to the national team. I kept that promise," he stressed. top.title: Ebonyi pensioners endorse Nwifuru for second term
top.description: By Jeff Agbodo, Abakaliki The Nigeria Union of Pensioners (NUP) has endorsed Ebonyi State Governor, Francis Nwifuru, for a second term in office ahead of the 2027 governorship election, citing his administration’s payment of outstanding pension and gratuity arrears dating back to 1996. The union also conferred an award on Nwifuru as the most pensioner-friendly governor in recognition of what it described as his commitment to the welfare of retired workers in the state. The endorsement was announced during the presentation of the award to the governor in Ebonyi State. The National President of NUP, Comrade Godwin Abumisi, represented by his deputy, Abdulahi Onuh, commended Nwifuru for clearing the backlog of pensions and gratuities owed to retired workers from 1996. Onuh described the achievement as significant, saying the governor had distinguished himself through his administration’s intervention in the welfare of pensioners. He said, “Clearing pensions and gratuity of pensioners from 1996 till date is not a small number of years. The Governor has written his name in gold. “While in Kano, I thought that the Governor of Kano State is number one. I never knew that coming to Ebonyi State, the Kano Governor will be number two. “To clear a backlog of pensions and gratuity from 1996 till date is a very big achievement. May God elongate the life of Ebonyi Governor. The Governor has done a lot.” He also commended the state government over plans to extend the state health insurance scheme to retirees, describing the initiative as another important intervention in their welfare. The NUP national leadership, however, urged the state government to implement pension increases and harmonisation of benefits, noting that pension increments were provided for under the Constitution. Onuh called on pensioners to reciprocate the governor’s gesture by voting for him in the 2027 election. He said, “You are indebted to the Governor. Use your PVCs and show him appreciation by voting for him in the 2027 general election. “When you go home, off your clothes and tell your children that as of two years back, they were taking you to the hospital every week. You were calling your children both home and abroad, bring me my medical allowance. “But the Governor has reduced the strength of your children in Nigeria and outside. Go and pay him back. Tell your children, tell your in-laws to pay the Governor back by voting for him.” Also speaking, the Ebonyi State Chairman of NUP, Comrade Anna Ibiam, said retired workers had endured years of unpaid pensions and gratuities before Nwifuru assumed office. top.title: At 44, England great James Anderson extends playing career with Surrey after shock Lancashire departure
top.description: At 44, James Anderson is not ready to walk away from cricket. England's legendary fast bowler is set to begin a new chapter in his illustrious career after joining Surrey for the 2027 county season, following the end of his 25-year association with Lancashire. Surrey confirmed the signing on Thursday, giving the veteran pacer an opportunity to continue playing at the highest level of county cricket. Anderson's move comes after Lancashire decided against renewing his contract for the upcoming season, bringing an unexpected end to his long association with his boyhood club. Despite the disappointment, Anderson has made it clear that he still has the hunger to compete, take wickets and contribute to a team's success. 'I still feel like I have a lot to offer': Anderson on Surrey move Anderson expressed his excitement about joining Surrey and said he was looking forward to contributing both on and off the field. "I still feel like I have a lot to offer, taking wickets, trying to help the team win games," Anderson said in a statement. The former England international also highlighted his desire to help younger players develop their skills and progress towards representing the national team. "I also think that I can bring a lot to the team off the field and help those young players who are looking to develop their skillset and go on and represent their country," he added. According to British media reports, Anderson has signed an initial one-year deal with Surrey, with an option to extend his stay beyond the 2027 season. Lancashire exit ends 25-year association Anderson's move to Surrey follows a difficult few weeks after Lancashire opted not to renew his contract. The decision ended a 25-year relationship with the county where he began his professional career in 2001. The veteran pacer admitted he was shocked by the decision but remained determined to explore new opportunities rather than bring his playing career to an end. His departure came despite an impressive 2026 County Championship campaign, during which he claimed 50 wickets. Anderson had also captained Lancashire during the season, making the decision not to retain him a significant development. The fast bowler will now bring his experience and leadership to Surrey as he looks to make an impact in the 2027 campaign. Anderson's remarkable international career Widely regarded as one of the greatest fast bowlers in cricket history, Anderson retired from international cricket in 2024 after a career spanning more than two decades. He finished with 991 international wickets across formats, the highest tally by a fast bowler in men's international cricket. His Test record remains particularly remarkable, with 704 wickets in 188 matches, making him the most successful fast bowler in the history of the format. Anderson also claimed 269 ODI wickets and 18 T20I wickets for England. He made his international debut in 2002 and became the spearhead of England's pace attack across several generations.

top.title: 'Everyone is thinking how is he going to get back in' - Alan Shearer names Arsenal summer signing as the Premier League's early player of the season
top.description: Liverpool v Arsenal FC - Premier League 2026/27 - Getty Images Sport Alan Shearer has named Ezri Konsa as the Premier League's player of the season so far, insisting the Arsenal summer signing has been so good that nobody has even noticed William Saliba's absence. The England defender has been an ever-present for Mikel Arteta's league leaders, and Saliba's looming return from a back injury now leaves the Gunners with a big selection call. Shearer crowns Konsa early player of the season Alan Shearer believes Konsa has been the standout performer in the Premier League this season after a superb start to life at Arsenal. The 29-year-old completed a £55 million move from Aston Villa in the summer, ending a seven-year spell at Villa Park that brought a Europa League triumph. Speaking to Betfair, Shearer said: "I think the player of the season up to now has been Ezri Konsa." Konsa has missed just one game so far, helping Arteta's side open up a five-point lead at the top of the table. Konsa makes Arsenal forget Saliba injury Arsenal signed Konsa partly to cover for Saliba, who returned from last summer's World Cup with a serious back injury. Instead, the England international has turned that absence into an afterthought for the reigning champions. Shearer added: "I just think when you look at the performances of Arsenal defensively, and look at his performances defensively, we haven't even really mentioned them missing William Saliba. The only time we've mentioned him is in the last two weeks and that's because everyone is thinking how is he going to get back in because Konsa has been that good." Ferdinand warns Arteta of a huge problem Rio Ferdinand recently made the same point on his YouTube channel: "Mikel Arteta has got a problem, he's got a huge problem now. What is he going to do when William Saliba is fit? Ezri Konsa has come into that back-four and he looks like he's been there for ten years." The former Manchester United defender added: "It's a problem but it's a problem that I hope Mikel Arteta will enjoy because he's got two top centre-backs vying to be in the team. It's a good position to be in. I think we will see Konsa sometimes playing right-back." Arsenal head to Newcastle as Brighton give chase Arsenal return from the international break with a tricky trip to Newcastle at St James' Park, with Saliba closing in on a comeback. Brighton, who have won seven of their 10 league games, sit second. Shearer expects them to stay the course. "Brighton could be Arsenal's main challenge to the title this season," he said. "I don't think they're going to go away."

top.title: How Jason Wilcox dealt with reckless Lisandro Martinez after his public outburst
top.description: How Jason Wilcox dealt with reckless Lisandro Martinez after his public outburst Manchester United head coach Michael Carrick secured a third-place finish and helped Manchester United return to the Champions League. However, the club’s hierarchy ruined all the momentum during the summer transfer window, overseeing a botched-up midfield rebuild and overlooking their abysmal defence. The defeat against Hull City in the Premier League opener teased what was to come, and the outburst following the loss at Atlético Madrid highlighted that Carrick is no longer in control of the ship. Jason Wilcox reprimanded Lisandro Martínez Manchester United’s first real test in the Champions League after nearly a three-year absence came against Atlético Madrid. A goal in the very first minute in the Spanish capital underlined the gulf between United and Europe’s elite. The Red Devils spent most of the night ball-watching or ball-chasing, saw Leny Yoro get sent off, and conceded another. Lisandro Martinez chose to show his intensity off the pitch, as he launched a “blistering tirade” at Jason Wilcox, Manchester United’s director of football, and INEOS over their transfer business. The Argentine was not wrong, but that certainly was not the right place to air behind-the-scenes frustrations. According to The Telegraph , Martínez was fined and apologised publicly and is thought to have been given a serious dressing-down in private by Wilcox over the rant. “Martínez was put in his place,” one source told the publication. The Telegraph added that several people internally felt that the outburst was rich coming from a player who had spent so much time on the sidelines since signing in 2022 and, in the words of one source, was “playing abysmally” and pointed to his contractual situation. Signed from Ajax, the Argentina international is out of contract at United next summer and is expected to depart. Dressing room without leaders The report claims that around the time of that Atlético defeat there were “growing doubts among the first-team staff about whether they could halt the slide.” There was concern that United’s squad was “badly lacking not just in terms of physicality, pace and aggression, but also natural leaders and players with aura and presence.” A week later, United proved their doubters right by succumbing to a 4–1 defeat to Como, who were playing in the Champions League for the first time in their history. According to the report, after this match, it was Bruno Fernandes’ turn to show the world that Carrick’s project is on the brink of collapsing, as the captain publicly questioned the head coach’s approach. He was subsequently dropped to the bench against Bournemouth, who beat the Red Devils 3–0 at Old Trafford.

top.title: Miami Heat’s Vice City Jerseys Are The Ultimate GTA VI Flex
top.description: Credit: Jim Rassol-Imagn Images The Miami Heat did not just release new jerseys, according to Sports Illustrated . They launched a full-scale event tied to the biggest video game launch in history. Grand Theft Auto VI drops on November 19th, and the team is ready to match that energy. The Heat will debut special-edition Vice City kits the night before the game starts. This happens when they face the Milwaukee Bucks. Outlaw Vibes on the Court Keshad Johnson knows exactly what this means for the fans. He grew up sneaking away to play the game in Oakland. “It caused some fights between me and him on turns,” Johnson says about his brother Kenny. The new uniforms capture that same feeling. They are all black with bright pink accents that look like neon signs. Hidden inside the letters and numbers is a map of Miami streets. Johnson called the look an “outlaw type vibe” in an interview with GQ. That is the exact feeling the team wants to project. The jerseys were designed by Nike and Travis Scott’s Cactus Jack brand. Their logos appear on both the shirts and the shorts. Details like these show the franchise is serious about this crossover. “My whole family is trying to get a Vice City jersey,” Johnson said when we spoke last weekend. Jennifer Alvarez, the Miami Heat Chief Creative Officer, sees the bigger picture. “We’re bringing sports and entertainment together in a way that’s never been done,” she told GQ. She added that the team aims to deliver an experience no one has had at an NBA game before. This is not just a uniform swap. It is a total immersion into the game’s world. Bringing Vice City to Life The Kaseya Center will transform into the video game itself. The plaza will feature a light-blue Ferrari and a turquoise Chevrolet Monte Carlo. These are just two of the cars players can drive in the game. A large sign on top of the arena will read “Welcome to Vice City.” The effort required to build this setup is massive. The helicopter was there to help install the sign. Fans attending the game on Wednesday night can buy the jerseys at the arena. They can also order burgers from Burger Shot. This is a rare chance to step inside a fictional world that feels real. The Heat are betting that Miami fans will embrace this connection. Johnson noted that the city has its own fashion culture. Bam Adebayo agrees that Vice City has a unique style. The Heat are leaning into that local identity while tapping into a global gaming audience. Now, only Rockstar Games and the Heat can pull off the event. The game launches on November 19th, but the celebration starts the night before.

top.title: From Talking Drums to Tourism Diplomacy: How Nigeria Captured Attention at WTM London 2026
top.description: With NTDA leading the national delegation, NTT Global Destinations mobilising international partnerships and diaspora networks, and NANTA representing Nigeria’s private tourism sector, the Nigeria Pavilion became a vibrant celebration of culture, community and tourism opportunities. For three exciting days, Nigeria brought its rhythm, culture, hospitality and entrepreneurial spirit to the global stage at World Travel Market (WTM) London 2026, held from 3 to 5 November at ExCeL London. Led by the Nigerian Tourism Development Authority (NTDA), under its Director General, Dr Olayiwola Awakan, the Nigeria Pavilion welcomed international visitors, tourism professionals, Nigerians and Africans living in the United Kingdom, and industry stakeholders who travelled from Nigeria. Supporting the national showcase was NTT Global Destinations (NGD), NTDA’s Strategic and Pavilion Implementation Partner, responsible for coordinating the exhibition’s planning, stakeholder engagement, international liaison and delivery. Together with the National Association of Nigeria Travel Agencies (NANTA) and diaspora media partners, Nigeria created an experience that extended beyond destination marketing. Day One: Nigeria Arrives in Colour and Rhythm The opening day brought the Nigeria Pavilion to life with traditional talking drums, cultural performances, networking and opportunities for visitors to experience Nigeria’s creative identity. From the energetic rhythms to conversations about Nigeria’s tourism offering, the pavilion quickly became a gathering point for visitors interested in discovering more about the country. Among the highlights was the opportunity to connect Nigerian culture with the global appeal of Nollywood, Afrobeats and contemporary African creativity. The Director General Who Stole the Show Perhaps one of the most memorable moments came when NTDA Director General, Dr Olayiwola Awakan, joined the traditional drummers and dancers in an energetic cultural performance. Rather than remaining a spectator, the DG became part of the attraction, embracing the rhythm and excitement of the Nigerian showcase. His performance drew attention and captured the spirit of the exhibition: a country confidently presenting its culture to the world. It was tourism diplomacy in its most authentic form, demonstrating that sometimes the most powerful way to promote a destination is simply to experience and celebrate it. Day Two: Tourism, Tradition and Private Sector Connections The second day combined cultural discovery with industry engagement, featuring a traditional palm wine experience, networking and interactions between Nigerian tourism stakeholders and international visitors. top.title: Penn State holds key advantages over Minnesota’s defense
top.description: Penn State’s offense is officially fun to watch again. The unit has put together back-to-back strong performances — although it hit a lull in the second half last week — against the Purdue Boilermakers and Washington Huskies . The most exciting part about the scoring uptick is that it has happened without wide receiver Koby Howard . Quarterback Rocco Becht finally looks comfortable playing against Big Ten competition, and it has paid off in a big way for the Nittany Lions . However, they won’t have a cakewalk this week, as Minnesota has one of the better defenses in the conference. It only allows 20.5 points per game, and it is just below the Nittany Lions in terms of yardage allowed, currently giving up 305 yards per game. Let’s compare Penn State’s offense to Minnesota’s defense and see who has the edge. Yards per carry Penn State offense: 4.15 yards per carry Minnesota defense: 3.88 yards per carry These numbers suggest that the blue and white have a mediocre running game and Minnesota has an excellent run defense. However, the Nittany Lions have been running the ball much more effectively lately, and they could pose a threat this weekend. Penn State’s running backs have been averaging 6.2 yards per carry over the last two games. The rushes have been much more explosive, and the running backs are finding yards more consistently in the power running game. This type of balance between the run and the pass could give the team an advantage going into Week 11. Time of possession Penn State offense: 32 minutes Minnesota defense: 29 minutes These two teams have nearly identical average times of possession. This could mean that whoever is able to establish the run and control the game will have a strong chance of winning. We just saw Penn State own the time of possession battle against Purdue a couple of weeks ago, and it resulted in a 31-17 victory that felt a lot bigger than what the scoreboard suggested. It’ll be hard to get to 43 minutes of possession again, but keeping Minnesota’s defense on the field will be key. Fourth-down conversions Penn State offense: 77.8% conversion rate Minnesota defense: allow 55.6% conversion rate The fourth-down battle is something Penn State should always have the edge in, as it converts 77.8% of its attempts. The Nittany Lions have been great at converting these short-yardage situations, and it really helps to give the offense second and third chances to stay on the field. Conversely, the Golden Gophers struggle with stopping teams on fourth down. Getting an extra set of downs when you would have normally punted also keeps your offense on the field longer, circling back to the time of possession battle. If Penn State wins this area of the game, then it can kill two birds with one stone. Follow Nittany Lions Wire on X and Facebook . nigeria.title: Ebonyi pensioners endorse Nwifuru for second term
nigeria.description: By Jeff Agbodo, Abakaliki The Nigeria Union of Pensioners (NUP) has endorsed Ebonyi State Governor, Francis Nwifuru, for a second term in office ahead of the 2027 governorship election, citing his administration’s payment of outstanding pension and gratuity arrears dating back to 1996. The union also conferred an award on Nwifuru as the most pensioner-friendly governor in recognition of what it described as his commitment to the welfare of retired workers in the state. The endorsement was announced during the presentation of the award to the governor in Ebonyi State. The National President of NUP, Comrade Godwin Abumisi, represented by his deputy, Abdulahi Onuh, commended Nwifuru for clearing the backlog of pensions and gratuities owed to retired workers from 1996. Onuh described the achievement as significant, saying the governor had distinguished himself through his administration’s intervention in the welfare of pensioners. He said, “Clearing pensions and gratuity of pensioners from 1996 till date is not a small number of years. The Governor has written his name in gold. “While in Kano, I thought that the Governor of Kano State is number one. I never knew that coming to Ebonyi State, the Kano Governor will be number two. “To clear a backlog of pensions and gratuity from 1996 till date is a very big achievement. May God elongate the life of Ebonyi Governor. The Governor has done a lot.” He also commended the state government over plans to extend the state health insurance scheme to retirees, describing the initiative as another important intervention in their welfare. The NUP national leadership, however, urged the state government to implement pension increases and harmonisation of benefits, noting that pension increments were provided for under the Constitution. Onuh called on pensioners to reciprocate the governor’s gesture by voting for him in the 2027 election. He said, “You are indebted to the Governor. Use your PVCs and show him appreciation by voting for him in the 2027 general election. “When you go home, off your clothes and tell your children that as of two years back, they were taking you to the hospital every week. You were calling your children both home and abroad, bring me my medical allowance. “But the Governor has reduced the strength of your children in Nigeria and outside. Go and pay him back. nigeria.title: Reps threaten action against Science Minister over bill
nigeria.description: By Gift ChapiOdekina, Abuja The House of Representatives has threatened legislative action against the Minister of Innovation, Science and Technology, Dr Kingsley Tochukwu Udeh, over his failure to attend a public hearing on a bill seeking to establish a National Research and Innovation Development Fund. The lawmakers warned that the ministry’s absence could delay the proposed legislation and undermine President Bola Tinubu’s efforts to attract international research grants and funding from development partners, donor agencies, United Nations organisations and Nigerians in the diaspora. The House Committee on Science and Technology expressed displeasure that neither the minister nor the ministry’s Permanent Secretary or any senior representative attended the hearing, despite the ministry’s direct responsibility for the subject matter of the bill, HB 2821. The committee also noted that the proposed legislation was sponsored by the executive and transmitted to the National Assembly by President Tinubu. Speaking at the hearing, a member of the committee, Hon. Ahmed Usman Jaha, representing Chibok, Damboa and Gwoza Federal Constituency of Borno State, described the ministry’s absence as a possible act of sabotage against the working relationship between the executive and legislative arms of government. Jaha, who spoke on behalf of the committee, said it was difficult to understand why a ministry directly concerned with an executive-sponsored bill of national importance would fail to participate in its consideration. “Unfortunately, some members of the executive are by extension sabotaging this relationship. The reason why I call it sabotage is that I see no reason whereby the executive can present a bill to the House for consideration, and that bill has national importance, but the ministry responsible for it will not show up,” he said. He disclosed that the committee had invited the Ministers of Justice, Innovation, Science and Technology, Education, Environment, Agriculture and Food Security, Health, Livestock Development, and Industry, Trade and Investment, alongside other stakeholders, to contribute to the legislative process. However, none of the invited ministers attended the hearing. Jaha said the absence of the Science and Technology Minister was particularly concerning, insisting that either the minister or the Permanent Secretary should have appeared before the committee. “We are not averse to the Ministry of Justice and other ministries that are not directly linked to the bill. But our concern this time around is the Ministry of Science and Technology. If any minister may not have time to attend, they may end up sending representatives. But the Minister of Science and Technology himself, who is more or less the sponsor of the bill, or in a worst-case scenario, the Permanent Secretary, must show up,” he said. nigeria.title: Zamfara commissioner dies at 50, governor mourns
nigeria.description: By Idris Salisu, Gusau Zamfara State Governor, Dauda Lawal, has mourned the death of the state’s Commissioner for Commerce, Tasiu Musa Shinkafi, who died on Wednesday at the age of 50. Shinkafi reportedly died in a hospital in Kaduna following a brief illness. In a condolence message, Lawal described his death as an irreparable loss to the state government, his family and the people of Zamfara. The governor said, “With heavy hearts and in total submission to the will of Almighty Allah (T), we received the shocking news of the passing of the Commissioner for Commerce, Tasiu Musa Shinkafi. “Tasiu’s death is a great loss not only to his family and the state government, but also to the people of Zamfara. “He will be remembered for his dedication, honesty, and commitment to Zamfara State.” Lawal recalled that Shinkafi had previously served as Commissioner for Youth and Sport before his redeployment to the Ministry of Commerce. Describing the deceased as a valued member of his administration and a brother in service, the governor said his contributions to governance, politics and public service would be remembered. He prayed to Almighty Allah to forgive the deceased’s shortcomings and grant his family the strength to bear the loss. nigeria.title: Oyo SDP candidate sues INEC over omission from list
nigeria.description: By Adeola Badru The governorship candidate of the Social Democratic Party (SDP) in Oyo State, Olusegun Agboola, has dragged the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) before the Federal High Court in Abuja over the omission of his name from the commission’s list of candidates for the 2027 governorship election. Agboola alleged that unnamed political interests were behind his exclusion, describing the development as illegal, inexplicable and politically motivated. The SDP candidate, who maintained that he had fulfilled all the necessary electoral requirements, said he was seeking a court order compelling INEC to include his name on the list. In a statement on Thursday, Agboola expressed concern over what he described as the selective omission of his name despite his qualification to contest the election. He said, “The illegal and unexplainable omission of my name from the latest INEC published list as the SDP governorship candidate for Oyo State is perplexing. “Of all qualified candidates, my name was singled out and omitted from the published list without any reason from INEC.” Agboola alleged that the omission was an attempt to weaken the SDP’s political standing ahead of the election, claiming that some politicians in rival parties were uncomfortable with the party’s agenda and positions on issues affecting the state. He said, “I have been told that some people from other popular parties are behind it. They are not comfortable with all we stand for, so they want to use INEC to diminish our campaign and suppress all our efforts.” Expressing confidence in the judicial process, the candidate said he expected the court to compel INEC to correct the omission, questioning why he had to seek legal intervention after complying with the prescribed procedures. “We have followed due process and the court will soon mandate INEC to include our names, but why is that necessary?” he queried. He further alleged that his exclusion was part of a broader attempt by unnamed political interests to manipulate the electoral process and influence the outcome of the 2027 governorship election. “Some people want to use every means possible to doctor the outcome. This is sad for our democracy and shows the integrity of the umpire is damaged if this anomaly is not loudly corrected with a very public announcement from the INEC chairman,” he added. Agboola said Oyo State needed practical and sustainable solutions to unemployment, insecurity, inadequate infrastructure and other socio-economic challenges. He argued that addressing the problems required deliberate, systemic and long-term interventions rather than temporary measures. nigeria.title: Armed robbers steal goods worth 1mn euros in Paris jewellery heist
nigeria.description: Armed robbers stole goods worth more than one million euros ($1.1 million) from a De Beers jewellery store in Paris Thursday before fleeing on scooters, authorities and a police source told AFP. The suspects, carrying long guns, targeted the store in the city’s 2nd arrondissement at around 11:00 am (1000 GMT). During the robbery, they brandished their weapons but did not open fire, and no one was injured, according to the Paris police. A police source estimated the value at more than one million euros, confirming an earlier report by French broadcaster Europe 1. Four suspects in balaclavas, one armed with an assault rifle, are believed to have fled on motorbikes towards the motorway, according to the same source, who spoke on condition of anonymity. The Paris police said it has deployed significant resources to track down the perpetrators. The organised crime unit has opened an investigation into “armed robbery by an organised gang”, the prosecutor’s office said. nigeria.title: Politicians deceive voters to win elections – Kukah
nigeria.description: The Catholic Bishop of Sokoto Diocese, Matthew Kukah, has accused politicians of making unrealistic promises during election campaigns to secure votes, rather than preparing Nigerians for the realities and challenges of governance. Kukah said politicians often deploy attractive images, grand promises and appealing narratives to sell voters a vision of a better society, only to abandon their commitments after assuming office and begin offering excuses for their inability to deliver. He spoke on Thursday in Abuja at a public symposium organised by the National Institute for Legislative and Democratic Studies (NILDS) in collaboration with The Kukah Centre. To illustrate the disconnect between campaign promises and governance, Kukah narrated the story of a politician who used impressive images of tarred roads, bridges, beautiful houses and children in smart school uniforms to persuade voters during his campaign. According to him, the politician won the election, but three years later, residents complained that none of the promised projects had been executed. When confronted, the politician reportedly told them: “You are confusing campaign with governance. What I did was purely a simple campaign. Governance is a difficult part.” Kukah said the response reflected a recurring pattern in Nigeria’s political system, where politicians make ambitious promises to win elections but resort to excuses after taking office. He said, “And this is why we have Nigerian politicians turn around, once they have been sworn in and after telling us all the things they want to do, and say, ‘We didn’t know that the treasury was so empty.’ Then, they start giving one excuse after the other.” The bishop argued that politicians were often more interested in creating attractive campaign narratives than communicating the realities of governance. He, however, said voters had a responsibility to interrogate political promises and assess their feasibility rather than accept campaign messages at face value. He stated, “The point I am making is that it is the business of politicians to seduce, deceive or tell us things we can’t do just to win our votes. But we are sufficiently knowledgeable, and our experience should help us to test the limits of the claims that politicians make.” Kukah urged Nigerians to develop the capacity to question politicians, scrutinise their proposals and demand accountability, stressing that citizens should not wait until elections are over before engaging the political elite. He also called for political choices that transcend ethnic, religious and class considerations. nigeria.title: FG concessions Port Harcourt airport for 30 years, eyes two others
nigeria.description: By Folarin Kehinde The Federal Government has signed a 30-year concession agreement for the Port Harcourt International Airport as part of efforts to attract private investment, improve operational efficiency and unlock the economic potential of the nation’s loss-making airports. The Minister of Aviation and Aerospace Development, Festus Keyamo, disclosed this on Thursday in Abuja during the signing of the concession agreement with Port Harcourt Airport Company Limited. Keyamo said the concession was aimed at improving the operational efficiency of the airport, boosting revenue generation and unlocking its commercial potential. He explained that the Federal Government had been using profits generated from major airports to subsidise the operations of other airports that were running at a loss. According to him, the cost of maintaining airports, including personnel expenses, diesel and other operational requirements, has continued to put pressure on government finances. The minister said government lacked the resources to fully develop the non-aeronautical components of some airports, making private sector participation necessary. “Some of our airports are being run at a loss. We make so much money from some of our primary airports, and most of those profits are ploughed into running other airports,” Keyamo said. He noted that the concession had the approval of President Bola Tinubu and the Federal Executive Council, adding that the process was not a sudden decision but one that successive administrations had struggled to implement. Keyamo said previous attempts to concession airports were frustrated by resistance from labour unions and court cases involving the government. He, however, attributed the successful conclusion of the process to negotiations with aviation unions, saying the government had secured their agreement before signing the deal. The minister assured workers that the concession would not lead to job losses or a reduction in their conditions of service. He said Tinubu had directed that the welfare of aviation workers must be protected throughout the concession process. “President Bola Tinubu was very concerned about that, that no worker should lose his job. The conditions of service should remain the same,” he said. Keyamo added that the concessionaire would be subjected to performance reviews every five years to ensure compliance with the terms of the agreement. He warned that the government could take back the airport if the concessionaire failed to meet the agreed standards. The minister also disclosed that the government had received proposals from investors interested in developing other airports, including those in Benin and Yola. He said the government was considering the proposals as part of efforts to make more airports commercially viable. nigeria.title: Tinubu: Wike inaugurates Rivers campaign council, directs it to recruit 5 new voters daily
nigeria.description: By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA: The Minister of the Federal Capital Territory FCT, Nyesom Wike, has inaugurated the Presidential Campaign Council for Rivers State and directed its members to recruit at least five new voters daily to deliver votes for President Bola Tinubu in the 2027 election. Wike, who performed the inauguration on Thursday, set a target of three million votes for the president in the state. He called for hard work, focus and issue-based campaigning, and dismissed recent confusion over appointments into the committees. “I am sure by Monday the list of the chairmen and members of the various sub-committees will have been prepared so that the chairmen can kick-start by inviting their various committee members. It is very important,” he said. The minister said victory in Rivers was not in doubt. “Everybody knows that we are going to win election in Rivers State. So we are not talking about winning now,” he said. Wike recalled how the three million figure came up in a discussion with Senate President Godswill Akpabio. “He said, ‘How much is the registered votes here?’ I said, ‘over three million.’ He said, ‘Okay, you will bring three million.’ I said, ‘Well, we will try’. I know that three million, if we work hard, it ia easy.” Wike urged members of the council to treat their appointments as an opportunity to work for the Rainbow Coalition, and called on them to stay united and disciplined in the face of provocation from the opposition. He cited the Olubadan and former governor of Oyo State, Oba Rasheed Ladoja who he said spoke a day earlier when the National Working Committee of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) paid him a courtesy visit in Oyo State. “He said if he was still in politics, if he was not a traditional ruler today, he would have joined Rainbow Coalition, that is the best way to bring every shade of opinion, members of other political parties to join hands to make sure that Mr. President is re-elected come 2027,” Wike said. Governor Siminalayi Fubara of Rivers State described the new council as bigger, wider and better coordinated than the structure that delivered victory for the president in 2023. He said former political adversaries had now closed ranks to work together for the state and the president. “Nothing is impossible. The only thing that is not possible is to revive the dead. If we take this as a serious task that must be achieved, we will come out decisively with a stronger vote than what we did in 2023,” Fubara said. The governor assured members who were left out that they would be accommodated in the subcommittees. He also warned against double-dealing and urged members to work with sincerity rather than profess loyalty in public while sabotaging the effort behind closed doors. “I am here, and I say it boldly anywhere, any day, in private and in secret: I have taken this position,” Fubara said. nigeria.title: Imo East: Court orders INEC to recognise Nwole as NDC candidate
nigeria.description: By Ikechukwu Nnochiri ABUJA – The Federal High Court in Abuja has ordered the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) to immediately recognise and publish the name of Uche Nwole as the candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) for the Imo East senatorial election scheduled for January 16, 2027. In a judgment delivered by Justice Mohammed Umar, the court said it was satisfied that the plaintiff, Nwole, was the bona fide winner of a primary election conducted by the party, which it noted was duly monitored by INEC. It held that, in view of Sections 84(1) and (2) and 86 of the Electoral Act 2026, the NDC ought to have nominated and forwarded the plaintiff’s name to the electoral body as its senatorial candidate. According to the court, the NDC could not lawfully nominate a consensus candidate other than the one who emerged from its INEC-monitored primary election. Consequently, aside from issuing an order of perpetual injunction restraining the party from nominating or submitting any other name for the election, the court barred INEC from accepting, listing or publishing any purported NDC candidate who allegedly emerged from a primary election that was never held or monitored by the commission, or any purported consensus candidate whose nomination breached Sections 87(1) and (3) of the Electoral Act 2026. The judgment followed suit number FHC/ABJ/CS/1225/2026, in which the NDC, INEC and Hon. Onyeagucha Uchechukwu were the 1st to 3rd defendants. The plaintiff alleged that although he secured the highest number of valid votes cast in the primary election, the party sidelined him and chose the 3rd defendant as its flag bearer for the senatorial poll. Justice Umar said that, after careful examination of all the evidence adduced in the matter, he was satisfied that the plaintiff’s case deserved to succeed. He therefore granted all seven principal reliefs the plaintiff sought. nigeria.title: Nigeria’s exports to China rise 81% to $2.25bn
nigeria.description: By Favour Ulebor, Abuja Nigeria’s exports to China rose by 81 per cent to $2.25 billion in the first half of 2026, while bilateral trade between both countries increased by 35 per cent to $17.4 billion, the Chinese Embassy has said. The Cultural Counsellor of the Chinese Embassy in Nigeria and Director of the China Cultural Centre in Nigeria, Mr Yang Jiaxing, disclosed this on Thursday in Abuja at the 2026 launch ceremony of the Voice of Nigeria (VON) China-Nigeria Bridge Programme. Yang attributed the growth to expanding economic cooperation between the two countries, saying China’s zero-tariff policy for 53 African countries, including Nigeria, which took effect in May 2026, would create more opportunities for Nigerian exports. He said China’s trade with African countries reached $207.4 billion in the first half of 2026, while imports from the continent rose to $28.5 billion between May and June. According to him, imports from Nigeria recorded year-on-year growth of more than 40 per cent in both May and June, reflecting stronger trade relations between the two countries. He said: “In the first half of this year, bilateral trade between China and Nigeria reached $17.4 billion, up 35 per cent year-on-year. China’s imports from Nigeria amounted to $2.25 billion, representing a remarkable increase of 81 per cent.” Yang described the China-Nigeria Bridge Programme as a platform for promoting cultural understanding, media cooperation and closer relations between citizens of both countries. The programme, jointly initiated by the Chinese Embassy, the Africa Regional Bureau of Xinhua News Agency and VON, provides Mandarin lessons and reports on China-Africa relations. Also speaking, the Director-General of VON, Jibrin Baba Ndace, said the introduction of Mandarin as the organisation’s ninth broadcast language would strengthen Nigeria’s international presence and enable it to communicate its stories to a wider audience. Ndace, who was represented by the Director of General Services, Alhaji Danladi Abubakar, said the service would promote Nigeria’s culture, tourism, business opportunities and national image among Chinese-speaking audiences. He said the initiative followed agreements reached between Nigeria and China at the 2024 Forum on China-Africa Cooperation held in Beijing. According to him, VON also signed agreements with Xinhua News Agency and the Chinese Embassy in 2026 to promote content sharing, staff training, broadcasting capacity and media cooperation. In his remarks, the Executive Secretary of the Nigeria Press Council, Dili Ezughah, described the programme as an important step towards strengthening cultural diplomacy and people-to-people relations. He urged the partners to sustain the initiative, saying its success should be measured by its ability to promote mutual understanding and lasting relationships between citizens of both countries. nigeria.title: Ododo flags off 38.5km Kogi road project
nigeria.description: …Promises to End Decades of Poor Access By Soni Daniel, Northern Region Editor Kogi State Governor, Alhaji Ahmed Usman Ododo, on Thursday flagged off the construction of the 38.5-kilometre Kabba–Olle-Bunu–Iluke-Bunu Road in Kabba/Bunu Local Government Area, promising to address decades of poor road infrastructure in the area. The project, flagged off at Oke-Ofin, is expected to improve connectivity among communities in Bunu land, ease the movement of agricultural produce and expand access to economic opportunities. Speaking at the ceremony, Ododo described the project as the fulfilment of a long-standing aspiration of the people, assuring residents that his administration would not abandon any community, irrespective of its location. He said the road would mark a new chapter for the area by reconnecting communities that had remained isolated for years. The governor recalled how the deplorable condition of the road had affected farmers, businesses and residents, explaining that farmers struggled to transport their produce to markets, while indigenes living outside the state found it difficult to visit their ancestral homes. He disclosed that his personal experience during a visit to Iluke-Bunu following a security incident involving students had strengthened his resolve to rehabilitate the road. nigeria.description: Dozens of cocaine packages piled up, weighing in at four tonnes and valued at $317 million — the seizure by Liberian police in July was a stark symbol of west Africa’s expanding role in the global cocaine trade. In recent years, the region has become a favoured route for traffickers moving drugs from producing countries in South America to Europe, where the highly lucrative cocaine market has exploded. Drug trafficking is now “one of the greatest threats” facing Liberia, President Joseph Boakai said in a national address in August, after several large-scale seizures. “Drugs are destroying young lives, weakening families, fuelling violence,” he warned. Politics has been tarnished too. Following the major drugs busts, former Liberian vice president Jewel Howard-Taylor was arrested for alleged involvement in an international drug trafficking network. But Liberia is by no means unique — the drugs trafficking scourge is region-wide. – Regional scourge – In neighbouring Sierra Leone, one of Europe’s most wanted cocaine traffickers, the convicted fugitive Dutchman Jos Leijdekkers, is operating with apparent support from the highest echelons of power, according to law enforcement, local testimonies and court documents gathered by AFP. “All the states in west Africa are vulnerable to cocaine trafficking,” Lucia Bird, west Africa director at the Global Initiative Against Transnational Organized Crime (GI-TOC), told AFP. “The region is perfectly positioned between the cultivation areas in Latin America and consumption markets, particularly in Europe,” she said. A GI-TOC report published in March spotlighted the issue. Around 30 percent of the drug consumed in 2025 in Europe went through west Africa, according to estimates in the report. But the true scale of the trafficking remains unknown — it is difficult to quantify given its illegal nature and the analysis of seizures is not a reliable indicator. – Maritime route – Several factors have contributed in recent years to the growing importance of the west Africa route, which is largely maritime. With improvements to its port infrastructure and road networks, west Africa has become more attractive to traffickers and its ports increasingly well-connected hubs. Although transporting drugs via the region takes longer and is more expensive, “the risk of having your product seized is lower”, Bird told AFP. As Europe has tightened its controls on ships coming from South America, cargoes originating in west Africa attract less scrutiny from European customs. But with west Africa increasingly seen as high-risk, Bird said perceptions and security measures were starting to change. – Overspill – As in other regions, cocaine trafficking fuels corruption among local elites and political decision-makers. Gemini declined to comment. A spokesperson for KAST would not discuss the transaction, but said the company is actively looking at acquisitions as its revenue and footprint grow. Neither firm has issued a public confirmation of a sale, and no regulator has announced a change-of-control approval. The disposal, if confirmed, would close a retreat Gemini laid out in February. On Feb. 4, the Nasdaq-listed company, known as Gemini (GEMI), approved a plan to exit and wind down its operations in the United Kingdom, the European Union and other European jurisdictions, and Australia, as part of a broader effort to cut expenses and support a path to profitability. It said it would keep operating in the United States and Singapore. The plan included a reduction in force of up to 200 employees in Europe, the United States and Singapore, or about 25% of Gemini’s global workforce as of that date. The company estimated about $11 million in pre-tax restructuring charges, mostly in cash, and said it expected the wind-down to be substantially completed in the first half of 2026. Reuters reported the job cuts the same day. Gemini later told U.K., European Economic Area and Australian customers that their accounts would close on April 6, with withdrawals-only starting in early March. sports.description: Michael Carrick has paid the price for Manchester United's disastrous start to the season (Oli SCARFF) Manchester United sacked manager Michael Carrick on Thursday after their worst-ever start to a Premier League campaign, with USA boss Mauricio Pochettino widely tipped to replace him. Former United captain Carrick led the team to an impressive third-place finish last season, but they have taken just eight points from 10 games in the current campaign and are in the relegation zone. The club confirmed in a statement that it had parted ways with the 45-year-old, following mounting speculation he would be axed during the international break. "After a disappointing start to the season, the club has come to the extremely difficult conclusion that a change is necessary in order to achieve our ambitions," United's statement said. "Michael is, and always will be, a Manchester United legend. Just as he did as a player, he has conducted himself with the highest standards of dedication and professionalism throughout his time back with the club." United said they intended to appoint a permanent successor "as quickly as possible". - Chaos - Carrick impressed after taking over as interim boss following Ruben Amorim's acrimonious exit in January, leading United to Champions League qualification. He was rewarded with a two-year permanent deal but, hampered by the club's underwhelming recruitment in the summer transfer window, his side have endured a steep decline this season. Carrick has struggled to maintain discipline, dropping captain Bruno Fernandes after he criticised his manager's tactics following a 4-1 thrashing at Champions League debutants Como. And defender Lisandro Martinez spoke out against the club's hierarchy over their lack of top-quality signings. Carrick's final game in charge was a chaotic 4-4 draw against Aston Villa on Sunday, after which he stressed he would not walk away. United, however, have decided to act in the hope of saving their season after a paltry three wins from 15 games in all competitions. It is believed Carrick's future was decided on Wednesday during a meeting in Monaco involving co-owner Jim Ratcliffe, chief executive Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox. Ex-Newcastle boss Eddie Howe and Julian Nagelsmann, most recently in charge of Germany, were touted as possible replacements but Pochettino has now emerged as the overwhelming favourite to succeed Carrick. The Argentine has extensive experience of the Premier League following spells in charge of Southampton, Tottenham and Chelsea, and he also coached Paris Saint-Germain. sports.title: Marlon Gomes: “Brazil have always been my second home”
sports.description: Marlon Gomes: “Brazil have always been my second home” For someone who faithfully represented Brazil from the ages of 15 to 20, a two-year absence may have felt like an eternity. Between 2019 and 2024, Marlon Gomes played for Brazil’s Under-16, Under-17, Under-18, Under-20 and Under-23 teams. With that kind of history, the path to the senior national team seems natural. Called up for the first time, the midfielder—matured by his journey “in his second home,” by overcoming the challenges of becoming a father at 15, and by the resilience needed to stay focused while playing in a country at war—now finds himself on the team he has always dreamed of playing for. “I spent a lot of time here, going back to the youth teams. I started coming to the national team at 15, so it has always been my second home. Whenever there was a call-up, I was there, along with Andrey. I have many friends I’ve known since the youth teams, and I’m very happy to see them again and to return (to the national team) after a long time, now with the senior team,” he said at a press conference on Thursday (12). Playing for Brazil, the Rio de Janeiro native won the South American Under-20 Championship and competed in the Under-20 World Cup and the CONMEBOL Pre-Olympic Tournament, as well as international friendly tournaments. Marlon Gomes at a press conference in Singapore during his first call-up to Brazil’s senior national team Credits: Rafael Ribeiro/CBF Experienced at youth international level, this time he is one of the newcomers among the 25 players selected by Carlo Ancelotti for the friendlies against Japan and Singapore. “I’m happy about this new project to bring fresh faces into the national team. I’m very happy, and my expectations about returning to the Brazilian national team couldn’t be higher. Now I’m fulfilling a dream with the senior team and being part of this new cycle. I have the highest hopes. This is my first time here. I hope to train well and learn as much as possible from the big-name players, and I hope I can play well so I can come back more often,” he said. A father at 15 A product of Vasco’s youth system, which he joined in 2017, Marlon Gomes became a father at a young age. His daughter Maitê was born when he was 15—a challenging age for someone who would have to balance fatherhood, the daily demands of football training and travel, and the dream of changing his family’s life. Despite the difficulties, he was determined to keep the promise he made to his mother and his daughter’s mother to grow personally and professionally. "I was very young and didn’t have the financial means. When my mother found out, we all cried together: me, her and my daughter’s mother. I promised to change our lives, and not just with empty words, but by becoming a great player and a respectable young man who would make it to the national team. I kept that promise," he stressed. sports.title: At 44, England great James Anderson extends playing career with Surrey after shock Lancashire departure
sports.description: At 44, James Anderson is not ready to walk away from cricket. England's legendary fast bowler is set to begin a new chapter in his illustrious career after joining Surrey for the 2027 county season, following the end of his 25-year association with Lancashire. Surrey confirmed the signing on Thursday, giving the veteran pacer an opportunity to continue playing at the highest level of county cricket. Anderson's move comes after Lancashire decided against renewing his contract for the upcoming season, bringing an unexpected end to his long association with his boyhood club. Despite the disappointment, Anderson has made it clear that he still has the hunger to compete, take wickets and contribute to a team's success. 'I still feel like I have a lot to offer': Anderson on Surrey move Anderson expressed his excitement about joining Surrey and said he was looking forward to contributing both on and off the field. "I still feel like I have a lot to offer, taking wickets, trying to help the team win games," Anderson said in a statement. The former England international also highlighted his desire to help younger players develop their skills and progress towards representing the national team. "I also think that I can bring a lot to the team off the field and help those young players who are looking to develop their skillset and go on and represent their country," he added. According to British media reports, Anderson has signed an initial one-year deal with Surrey, with an option to extend his stay beyond the 2027 season. Lancashire exit ends 25-year association Anderson's move to Surrey follows a difficult few weeks after Lancashire opted not to renew his contract. The decision ended a 25-year relationship with the county where he began his professional career in 2001. The veteran pacer admitted he was shocked by the decision but remained determined to explore new opportunities rather than bring his playing career to an end. His departure came despite an impressive 2026 County Championship campaign, during which he claimed 50 wickets. Anderson had also captained Lancashire during the season, making the decision not to retain him a significant development. The fast bowler will now bring his experience and leadership to Surrey as he looks to make an impact in the 2027 campaign. Anderson's remarkable international career Widely regarded as one of the greatest fast bowlers in cricket history, Anderson retired from international cricket in 2024 after a career spanning more than two decades. He finished with 991 international wickets across formats, the highest tally by a fast bowler in men's international cricket. His Test record remains particularly remarkable, with 704 wickets in 188 matches, making him the most successful fast bowler in the history of the format. Anderson also claimed 269 ODI wickets and 18 T20I wickets for England. He made his international debut in 2002 and became the spearhead of England's pace attack across several generations.

sports.title: 'Everyone is thinking how is he going to get back in' - Alan Shearer names Arsenal summer signing as the Premier League's early player of the season
sports.description: Liverpool v Arsenal FC - Premier League 2026/27 - Getty Images Sport Alan Shearer has named Ezri Konsa as the Premier League's player of the season so far, insisting the Arsenal summer signing has been so good that nobody has even noticed William Saliba's absence. The England defender has been an ever-present for Mikel Arteta's league leaders, and Saliba's looming return from a back injury now leaves the Gunners with a big selection call. Shearer crowns Konsa early player of the season Alan Shearer believes Konsa has been the standout performer in the Premier League this season after a superb start to life at Arsenal. The 29-year-old completed a £55 million move from Aston Villa in the summer, ending a seven-year spell at Villa Park that brought a Europa League triumph. Speaking to Betfair, Shearer said: "I think the player of the season up to now has been Ezri Konsa." Konsa has missed just one game so far, helping Arteta's side open up a five-point lead at the top of the table. Konsa makes Arsenal forget Saliba injury Arsenal signed Konsa partly to cover for Saliba, who returned from last summer's World Cup with a serious back injury. Instead, the England international has turned that absence into an afterthought for the reigning champions. Shearer added: "I just think when you look at the performances of Arsenal defensively, and look at his performances defensively, we haven't even really mentioned them missing William Saliba. The only time we've mentioned him is in the last two weeks and that's because everyone is thinking how is he going to get back in because Konsa has been that good." Ferdinand warns Arteta of a huge problem Rio Ferdinand recently made the same point on his YouTube channel: "Mikel Arteta has got a problem, he's got a huge problem now. What is he going to do when William Saliba is fit? Ezri Konsa has come into that back-four and he looks like he's been there for ten years." The former Manchester United defender added: "It's a problem but it's a problem that I hope Mikel Arteta will enjoy because he's got two top centre-backs vying to be in the team. It's a good position to be in. I think we will see Konsa sometimes playing right-back." Arsenal head to Newcastle as Brighton give chase Arsenal return from the international break with a tricky trip to Newcastle at St James' Park, with Saliba closing in on a comeback. Brighton, who have won seven of their 10 league games, sit second. Shearer expects them to stay the course. "Brighton could be Arsenal's main challenge to the title this season," he said. "I don't think they're going to go away."

sports.title: How Jason Wilcox dealt with reckless Lisandro Martinez after his public outburst
sports.description: How Jason Wilcox dealt with reckless Lisandro Martinez after his public outburst Manchester United head coach Michael Carrick secured a third-place finish and helped Manchester United return to the Champions League. However, the club’s hierarchy ruined all the momentum during the summer transfer window, overseeing a botched-up midfield rebuild and overlooking their abysmal defence. The defeat against Hull City in the Premier League opener teased what was to come, and the outburst following the loss at Atlético Madrid highlighted that Carrick is no longer in control of the ship. Jason Wilcox reprimanded Lisandro Martínez Manchester United’s first real test in the Champions League after nearly a three-year absence came against Atlético Madrid. A goal in the very first minute in the Spanish capital underlined the gulf between United and Europe’s elite. The Red Devils spent most of the night ball-watching or ball-chasing, saw Leny Yoro get sent off, and conceded another. Lisandro Martinez chose to show his intensity off the pitch, as he launched a “blistering tirade” at Jason Wilcox, Manchester United’s director of football, and INEOS over their transfer business. The Argentine was not wrong, but that certainly was not the right place to air behind-the-scenes frustrations. According to The Telegraph , Martínez was fined and apologised publicly and is thought to have been given a serious dressing-down in private by Wilcox over the rant. “Martínez was put in his place,” one source told the publication. The Telegraph added that several people internally felt that the outburst was rich coming from a player who had spent so much time on the sidelines since signing in 2022 and, in the words of one source, was “playing abysmally” and pointed to his contractual situation. Signed from Ajax, the Argentina international is out of contract at United next summer and is expected to depart. Dressing room without leaders The report claims that around the time of that Atlético defeat there were “growing doubts among the first-team staff about whether they could halt the slide.” There was concern that United’s squad was “badly lacking not just in terms of physicality, pace and aggression, but also natural leaders and players with aura and presence.” A week later, United proved their doubters right by succumbing to a 4–1 defeat to Como, who were playing in the Champions League for the first time in their history. According to the report, after this match, it was Bruno Fernandes’ turn to show the world that Carrick’s project is on the brink of collapsing, as the captain publicly questioned the head coach’s approach. He was subsequently dropped to the bench against Bournemouth, who beat the Red Devils 3–0 at Old Trafford.

sports.description: Credit: Jim Rassol-Imagn Images The Miami Heat did not just release new jerseys, according to Sports Illustrated . These are just two of the cars players can drive in the game. A large sign on top of the arena will read “Welcome to Vice City.” The effort required to build this setup is massive. The helicopter was there to help install the sign. Fans attending the game on Wednesday night can buy the jerseys at the arena. They can also order burgers from Burger Shot. This is a rare chance to step inside a fictional world that feels real. The Heat are betting that Miami fans will embrace this connection. Johnson noted that the city has its own fashion culture. Bam Adebayo agrees that Vice City has a unique style. The Heat are leaning into that local identity while tapping into a global gaming audience. sports.title: Penn State holds key advantages over Minnesota’s defense
sports.description: Penn State’s offense is officially fun to watch again. The unit has put together back-to-back strong performances — although it hit a lull in the second half last week — against the Purdue Boilermakers and Washington Huskies . The most exciting part about the scoring uptick is that it has happened without wide receiver Koby Howard . Quarterback Rocco Becht finally looks comfortable playing against Big Ten competition, and it has paid off in a big way for the Nittany Lions . However, they won’t have a cakewalk this week, as Minnesota has one of the better defenses in the conference. It only allows 20.5 points per game, and it is just below the Nittany Lions in terms of yardage allowed, currently giving up 305 yards per game. Let’s compare Penn State’s offense to Minnesota’s defense and see who has the edge. Yards per carry Penn State offense: 4.15 yards per carry Minnesota defense: 3.88 yards per carry These numbers suggest that the blue and white have a mediocre running game and Minnesota has an excellent run defense. However, the Nittany Lions have been running the ball much more effectively lately, and they could pose a threat this weekend. Penn State’s running backs have been averaging 6.2 yards per carry over the last two games. The rushes have been much more explosive, and the running backs are finding yards more consistently in the power running game. This type of balance between the run and the pass could give the team an advantage going into Week 11. Time of possession Penn State offense: 32 minutes Minnesota defense: 29 minutes These two teams have nearly identical average times of possession. This could mean that whoever is able to establish the run and control the game will have a strong chance of winning. We just saw Penn State own the time of possession battle against Purdue a couple of weeks ago, and it resulted in a 31-17 victory that felt a lot bigger than what the scoreboard suggested. It’ll be hard to get to 43 minutes of possession again, but keeping Minnesota’s defense on the field will be key. Fourth-down conversions Penn State offense: 77.8% conversion rate Minnesota defense: allow 55.6% conversion rate The fourth-down battle is something Penn State should always have the edge in, as it converts 77.8% of its attempts. The Nittany Lions have been great at converting these short-yardage situations, and it really helps to give the offense second and third chances to stay on the field. Conversely, the Golden Gophers struggle with stopping teams on fourth down. Getting an extra set of downs when you would have normally punted also keeps your offense on the field longer, circling back to the time of possession battle. If Penn State wins this area of the game, then it can kill two birds with one stone. Follow Nittany Lions Wire on X and Facebook . For Martin O’Neill’s side, even winning the Scottish Premiership would no longer guarantee a straightforward route into the Champions League. Instead, Celtic would enter at the second qualifying round, requiring them to negotiate three two-legged ties to reach the lucrative league phase. Without domestic cup success, Celtic would ordinarily enter the Conference League at the second qualifying round, although the identity of the Scottish Cup winners could alter that outcome. Should the Premiership champions also lift the Scottish Cup, the Europa League qualification place could instead pass to the league runners-up. The implications extend beyond Celtic’s European ambitions, with the club potentially facing competitive Champions League qualifiers as early as July. That would place additional pressure on the Celtic board to complete their summer recruitment business early, rather than allowing significant squad rebuilding to stretch into August.
